chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who rented land for one thousand dirhams, then subleased part of it for two hundred dirhams. Then the owner of the land who had leased it to him said, 'I will enter with you in it according to what you rented it for, and we will spend together, and whatever surplus is in it will be between me and you.' He said:
There is no harm in that.

key_terms.أَرْضًا: a piece of land being leased for use
key_terms.اسْتَأْجَرَ: rented or leased for a payment
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a monetary unit used to specify the lease amount
key_terms.فَنُنْفِقُ: we will jointly spend or bear expenses
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal objection; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh for a landowner to join a tenant in a profit-sharing arrangement after leasing the land?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a leasing arrangement involving agricultural land, subleasing, and a later profit-sharing partnership with the landowner. The Imam عليه السلام rules that such an arrangement is permissible, indicating no objection to this form of shared expenditure and profit division.
